system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

We need answer as AI legal assistant to buyer. Need review seller SPA positions vs buyer playbook. Need identify departures from playbook and pushback recommendations. Need produce material issues and reasoning, then summary recommendations. We must be careful: documents fictional. Need align with buyer's positions. Let's parse seller update and disclosure letter against playbook.

Playbook baseline: buy 100% Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24m price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

General Warranty cap starting 25% / AUD 6m; 20% / AUD 4.8m conditional fallback only with Amelia Frost written identifying draft; none given. Seller proposes 20% starting? Wait seller says aggregate liability limited to 20% of price being AUD 4,800,000. Playbook starting position 25%/6m, fallback 20% conditional. Seller's proposed clause 12.1 aggregate liability capped at 20% from first dollar? They say "limited to 20% of purchase price" not 25%. This conflicts: buyer doesn't accept 20% without principal approval. So need push back: reject 20% cap; insist on 25% starting, with fallback only if approved. Also if seller caps at 20%, not falling back. Need mention threshold de minimis / basket etc. Playbook de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000 seller liable from first dollar. Seller proposes de minimis 25,000, basket 250,000. Significant divergence: thresholds too high, buyer liable-from-first for too low amounts. Push back on clauses 12.2, maybe 13. Need note standard thresholds? But playbook internal. Also seller's limitation general claims 18 months after Completion, not 24. Playbook 24 standard, 18 fallback needing Amelia Frost approval none. Seller's proposed 18 months is a fallback without approval. Also fundamental/title same caps/time limits as general. Playbook fundamental separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years. Seller says administrative simplicity same. Push back: maintain separate regime and longer period. Limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance to all claims of any nature (clause 9.3/12.8/20.5) carved out fraud/wilful concealment. Playbook says carve out all caps, baskets, time, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to max enforceable; no one may waive. This likely consistent? Seller includes carve-outs? They say limitations apply to all Claims of any nature; doesn't explicitly exclude fraud, but likely standard. Need check disclosure: seller relies on general disclosure data room and public registers; playbook requires specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room/public-register deemed disclosure. Need push back on Schedule 7.

Buyer knowledge clause 8.3: buyer no claim matter of which buyer or advisers had knowledge including discoverable from data room or public records. Playbook delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnity. Seller's broad blanket deems disclosure sufficient. Need reject; require exceptions with named knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; cannot excuse title/capacity/fraud/specific indemnities. Also disclosure letter says "Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers." Conflict.

Bluefen consent: seller uses reasonable endeavour and treats consent satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent? Playbook requires effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient for material customer consent. Seller preamble says conditions addressed; clause 11.2 with conditions 11.3, uses reasonable endeavour. Disclosure letter says not included final written consent or evidence conditions satisfied. Need push back strongly: insist effective consent + evidence conditions satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavour insufficient. Could be risk: customer consent may change, conditions not met, representations. Need maybe accept consent only if final written consent obtained and conditions satisfied, perhaps with discharge. Don't accept on delivery. Also note Bluefen material ~3.6m FY26 revenue ~30%, significant. The "change-control consent" likely customer requires consent; reasonable efforts insufficient; need actual evidence.

Riverlark: seller proposes release following Completion. Playbook requires current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; post-completion release needs irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval. Seller's approach lacks current repayment, direct rep from completion funds, irrevocable undertaking; release after completion unacceptable. Need push back: include current repayment, direct Completion funds repayment, discharge effective security releases; if release after completion, require irrevocable undertaking (with buyer approval). Also noting facility outstanding ~3.2m.

Funds flow: DD-005 closing bonuses AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow silently excludes them. Seller acknowledges not separately itemised. Need push back: add DD-005 line items totaling AUD 420,000 and triggered on-costs, either explicitly paid by seller or seller-funded elsewhere; else price adjustment/deduction.

Ironquay IP: existing indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; playbook broaden narrow indemnity preserving SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified. Seller says adequate. Need push back: broaden to cover broader IP matters, preserve SOW3 cure but not undervalue; ensure DD-010 not bank-independent? They say not independently verified, so buyer should treat as unresolved; maybe broader indemnity. Need compare: playbook wants broad indemnity, preserve SOW3 cure, AUD 180k not verified. Seller narrows and calls adequate. Push back on scope and cost.

Export/privacy incident DD-006: seller says not expected material; no confirmed breach. Playbook requires logs, investigate, updates; assume no confirmed breach? Actually playbook says assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction? Let's parse: "Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction." Hmm phrase odd: "assume no confirmed breach... in either direction." Means buyer shouldn't assume there is a breach; seller should prove none? Or we don't assume confirmed breach exists. There is a divergence: seller claims preliminary operational matter not expected material, no confirmed breach, no loss amount. Playbook wants specific fair disclosure, logs preserved, investigation updates. Seller might be too dismissive. However if "assume no confirmed breach", seller's letter says no breach and no loss amount, seems okay? Need determine: seller says "As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file..." It also says "no loss amount" and not characterize confirmed breach. Playbook: preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach/harm/notification duty/numeric demand in either direction. That means if seller says no breach, okay but buyer still wants logs, update, investigate; seller should disclose further investigation status. Also no numeric demand from seller. Could accept but require continued investigation and no de minimis? But playbook's requirement maybe material? Seller's threshold thresholds are high; if incident small, could be irrelevant. Need maybe push back on Schedule 7 and require updated disclosure. But need identify material issues. Let's not overstate; perhaps seller's statement aligns except want specific logs and ongoing. But playbook says "assume no confirmed breach..." Perhaps seller already says not confirmed. The main issue is disclosure framework general reliance vs specific. Need focus.

Office lease DD-007: seller identifies notification obligation but not landlord consent. Playbook no mention office lease; not necessarily issue unless landlord consent required. Maybe okay; but note if lease not appropriately discharged, needs consent? Not in playbook. We can ignore or note if disclosure omits sufficient relief. Not material relative to playbook. But question asks where do they depart from our playbook; office lease maybe not. Keep minimal.

Supplier renewals Sandbar AUD 330k: playbook assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. Seller treats ordinary-course. Since priced debt-free/cash-free, seller should disclose and buyer assess. No automatic classification/deduction needed but buyer can challenge if ordinary course. Could be okay if disclosed; but "ordinary-course operating costs" without details maybe insufficient. Playbook says "assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction." Might be acceptable. Could push back on need to specify why each renewal ordinary course, accrued/terminable, timing. But maybe minor. Givenseller says "ordinary-course operating costs," enough? Buyer may want reasons.

Mossvale DD-009 assignment restriction: not requiring consent merely because shares sold; playbook no mention. Note not necessarily departure. Maybe mention caution if Mossvale reps involved.

Tax/IP: seller considers settled under general regime. Playbook says Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. Seller assumes settled. Need push back: keep tax and IP warranties open, avoid assuming settled under general regime; treat no unlimited liability/resolution. Must not close. Also "general regime above" conflicts with playbook open terms. Need push back.

Title: seller evidences via Company share register at DD-012; playbook require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is supplied internal source, not independent proof. Seller says "identifies source relied on, does not state buyer completed own verification." Need push back: require independent evidence e.g. title opinions, beneficial ownership, encumbrance search, certificate of authority, basis of share register; do not rely solely on supplied internal register. Also "shares sold" note.

Fraud carve out: seller clause 9.3/12.8/20.5 limitations to all claims of any nature. Playbook says carve out fraud etc to maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive. Need check if seller includes carve out? It doesn't explicitly state fraud carve-out, but limitations apply all claims. Playbook likely expects explicit carve-out of fraud/wilful concealment. Seller may be standard. Could ask seller to explicitly exclude fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time, exclusive remedies, non-reliance. But "[STANDARD]" marked reviewed and cleared by both sides? The review note says focus OPEN only. Fraud carve-out is maybe standard? Playbook says "carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance ... to maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this." Seller's clause doesn't explicitly mention fraud. But standard SPAs often include fraud carve-out;seller marks [STANDARD]? Hmm not sure. We can mention if absent, require explicit carve-out.

Let's parse seller positions more systematically:

SELLER UPDATE KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS:
[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 General liability cap: aggregate liability limited to 20% of purchase price AUD 4,800,000.
Playbook: starting 25%/6m; 20% conditional fallback only Amelia Frost identifies draft none given. So seller position conflicts starting cap.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 Thresholds: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess recoverable.
Playbook: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000 seller liable from first dollar. Divergence.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3/13 Time limits: general warranty claims within 18 months after Completion; limitation applies generally.
Playbook: 24 months after Completion; 18 months fallback requiring Amelia Frost approval none. Seller proposed 18.

Fundamental/title: same caps/time as general. Playbook separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years. Divergence.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3/12.8/20.5 Limitations, exclusive remedies, non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature.
Playbook says carved out fraud etc maximum; no waiver. Seller no explicit carve-out. Maybe okay? Need examine clause wording. If limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance applies to all claims, that includes title/capacity fraud? But fraud is typically carve-out in standard; if not explicitly mentioned, maybe seller included common carve-out elsewhere? Seller doc doesn't show full clauses. "[STANDARD]" maybe both sides agreed. Playbook says carve out fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct to maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive. It likely is standard too. We can mention require explicit carve-out if not visible, and no waiver.

Disclosure Schedule 7: reliance on general disclosure data room and public registers. Playbook: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room/public-register deemed disclosure. Reject.

Clause 8.3 buyer knowledge: no claim matter buyer/advisers knew including discoverable from data room/public records. Playbook: delete blanket exclusions; qualifier named seller knowledge persons+reasonable enquiry; never excuse title/capacity/fraud/specific indemnity. Reject.

Conditions-Bluefen: "Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent." Playbook: effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavour alone insufficient for material customer consent. Strong pushback.

Riverlark: release following Completion. Playbook: current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases; post-completion release needs irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval. Seller proposal inadequate.

Funds flow: DD-005 bonuses not separately itemised. Playbook: specific line item or seller-funded; silent exclusion unacceptable.

Ironquay IP: narrow indemnity limited to SOW3 payment considered adequate. Playbook: broaden narrow indemnity preserving SOW3 cure; AUD 180k not independently verified. Reject.

Incident DD-006: preliminary operational matter not expected material. Playbook: preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach etc. Seller says no confirmed breach, no loss amount. But it may be too dismissive; need disclosure/update. However if playbook says assume no confirmed breach, maybe seller okay. But "preliminary operational matter not expected material" could reduce commitment to due diligence. Need push back: require logs preserved, full investigation disclosure and updates, and no matter possibly material until assessed. Also seller's "not expected material" might conflict with buyer expectations; not unconscionable if harmless, but should still update.

Supplier renewals: ordinary-course operating costs. Playbook assess; no automatic debt classification/price deduction. Acceptable but maybe ask for details. No need strong push.

Tax/IP: Seller considers settled under general regime. Playbook open terms. Reject assumption of settlement.

Title: share register evidence. Playbook require independent title evidence; DD-012 internal. Reject reliance solely on supplied register.

Additional: seller says "As at date of letter Seller has NOT included final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied." Need note pending and risk.

Also clause 12.1? Playbook says starting position 25%/AUD 6m. Seller says limited to 20% from first dollar. If buyer's 20% fallback only with prior written authorization from Amelia Frost identifying draft; none given. So seller should not include 20% unconditionally. Need push back: "Accept 25% starting cap; reserve the 20% fallback for approval by buyer principal Amelia Frost specifying draft; do not incorporate seller's unconditional 20% cap." Maybe ask seller to remove 20% unconditional. If seller insists 20% starting, say no.

Also thresholds: playbook de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000. Seller's 25k/250k are 5x and 5x. Even standard SaaS deals usually 1% basket, 10% cap, maybe 12-18 months. Buyer positions can differ. Need push back on thresholds; seller may argue market. But our playbook is internal. Include "if market terms differ, acceptable; our position is higher caps/thresholds for greater buyer protection; seller may not rely."

Time periods: 18 months is less favorable; require 24 standard; 18 only if approval. Seller maybe thinks administrative simplicity. Note shorter period disadvantages buyer.

Funding: debt-free/cash-free; Riverlark facility outstanding; withdrawals from completion funds should repay directly. If seller proposes post-completion release, buyer expects funds flow includes repayment; maybe seller notes facility to be addressed. But playbook demands effective release now, not later.

Employee bonuses: It says "DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply." Playbook says DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be specific line item or seller-funded. Seller acknowledges but no details. Need push back: include explicit line item for closing bonuses and for-on-costs, track fund flow, potentially price adjustment. Also "payroll tax/super/on-costs" important because costs flow through buyer obligations; if not itemized, silence likely unfair. Also sale price not adjusted? They said "price mechanics
